value.note: DELTA VERDICT: APPROVE — the blocker is fixed and independently verified in both directions. Fix sha b332f46e461ac9fd9706f249940502b5740ade67, reviewed detached in /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-review-013; round-1 sha was beee1491be13f3920affc5d257eb580974188360. f-9c41 FIXED: on the identical 12,000-nearer-foreign + 5-in-scope geometry the shipped statement now returns hits=5 / scanned=5 / admitted=5 at EVERY step of the 40->10,240 expansion sequence, byte-for-byte matching the pre-013 statement on the same corpus, where round 1 returned hits=0 with scanned==candidate_limit at every step and then raised candidate_limit_exhausted. f-2e07 FIXED and the new test genuinely discriminates: scoped_search_passes_twelve_thousand_nearer_foreign_vectors is green at b332f46 and RED against the pre-fix SQL spliced back in with a column-compatible admitted_count shim, failing behaviourally (left 0, right 5, SearchPage { hits: [], passes: 2, candidate_limit_exhausted: true }) rather than on a missing column. f-6a55 FIXED: the stale iterative_scan comment is gone. All four of the reviewer's binding precision notes are implemented as specified — admitted_sources relocated below the LIMIT, BOTH key legs inside it, a distinct scan_incomplete carrier set on all three SearchOutcome exits and surfaced in the HTTP envelope, and the no-Err change scoped to search_elements only (the sole remaining Err(candidate_limit_exhausted) is at embeddings.rs:413 inside the unfiltered query_embeddings). ac-0001 TRUE 5/5, ac-0002 TRUE, ac-0003 TRUE (store 53/53, daemon 56/56 — one more than round 1, a new starvation case). ac-0004/ac-0005 remain deferred: prod is still unbounced. CI on the sha reads gate pass in 6m3s; read, not rerun. Two round-1 MINORs remain open by design — f-7b13 and f-4d88 were not forwarded in the ruling — and this round adds one new MINOR (f-3b7e, proven) and one NIT (f-5c92). None is blocking. Performance moved sharply the right way: the plan-shape ANALYZE fell from 105.5-121.3 ms in round 1 to 6.873-7.315 ms here, because admitted_elements is now bounded to the candidate page instead of materialising the whole eligible elements set. All reviewer edits were uncommitted and reverted; git diff on crates/ is 0 lines. All work on flowspace3-db-test 127.0.0.1:5434; prod never touched. AMENDED 2026-09-02 after #101 merged as c2f4709, at o-prime's instruction: ac-0004 is now CHECKED (vd-ac04) on the strength of a single guarded read-only prod EXPLAIN taken before the bounce — 35.068 ms, 8,063 shared blocks, smart_content max Actual Loops 1, and the HNSW index still the childless <=>-ordered driver at 160 rows, i.e. all four thresholds including both reviewer-added clauses, with the scope limits carried verbatim. ac-0005 is split out as vd-ac05 and remains deferred pending the bounce. dim0-2b45 and vd-ac01 are amended: the reviewer's round-2 claim that smart_content is 'probed once per candidate' and that the plan's 'resolved ONCE' prose no longer held is WITHDRAWN — that was a fixture artefact, prod measures 1 loop. Backlog row 168 records the underlying fixture-realism problem. FURTHER AMENDED after the bounce: ac-0005 is now CHECKED (vd-ac05) — prod daemon pid 74144, binary identity confirmed functionally by the envelope carrying scan_incomplete and passes without candidate_limit_exhausted; eight interleaved runs, every threshold met, and the reviewer's must-return-results gate passing 8/8 with passes=1 on every run. With ac-0004 and ac-0005 both discharged, all five acceptance criteria are TRUE and the review is closed. Two MINORs (f-7b13, f-4d88) remain open by ruling as follow-up work. A second ac-0005 pass at load1 12.9 (against the first pass's 17.9-20.3) returned means of 0.580 s vs 0.629 s - 7.8% apart, inside noise - so the load coupling that motivated the bracketing protocol is no longer observable across sixteen runs.

value.finding: MEDIUM — a scan that genuinely ran to completion can be reported as scan_incomplete. expansion_decision (embeddings.rs:89-108) computes expansion_exhausted = admitted_stalled || expansion == MAX_CANDIDATE_EXPANSIONS, then scan_incomplete = hit_count < requested && expansion_exhausted. It never subtracts the case where the vector scan actually finished. When a pass both exhausts the candidate scan (scanned < candidate_limit, i.e. the index has no more rows to give) AND sees the admitted set stop growing on that same pass, both flags are true and the short page is labelled scan_incomplete even though nothing further exists to find. That is a false claim of incompleteness on an exhaustive answer, and it now propagates: crates/daemon/src/search.rs:502-508 branches on scan_incomplete to decide whether to suppress the generic filtered-empty steer, so a content-filtered search that legitimately matched nothing can be reported as a bounded short scan rather than an honest empty. It over-reports rather than under-reports, which is the safe direction, and it is exactly the inverse of the confident-lie failure search.rs:405-410 exists to prevent. Smallest fix: scan_incomplete = hit_count < requested && expansion_exhausted && !candidate_scan_exhausted. The one existing unit test (embeddings.rs:1037) covers only the ceiling case with a growing admitted set, so it cannot see this.
value.receipt: Proven, not reasoned. A disposable unit test asserting the correct value was added, run, and reverted: expansion_decision(1, 10, 100, 160, 5, Some(5), 3) — hit_count 1, requested 10, scanned 100, candidate_limit 160 (so the scan IS exhausted), admitted 5, previous_admitted Some(5) (so admitted stalled), expansion 3 (below the ceiling). Observed 'REVIEWER_EDGE: Return { scan_incomplete: true }'; assertion against Return { scan_incomplete: false } failed left/right as expected. Source restored; git diff on crates/ = 0 lines.

value.finding: The search envelope exposes two keys that can never differ. crates/daemon/src/search.rs:350-352 sets `let scan_incomplete = candidate_limit_exhausted;` from the single SearchPage flag, and crates/daemon/src/http.rs:620-622 publishes candidate_limit_exhausted, scan_incomplete and passes as three separate fields. Two of the three are aliases by construction, so an agent or client reading the envelope will reasonably infer a distinction that does not exist and may branch on it. Either publish one flag, or give them genuinely different meanings (for example candidate_limit_exhausted = the ceiling was reached, scan_incomplete = the answer is short for any bounded reason) — which is also the shape f-3b7e's fix would want, since 'ceiling reached' and 'answer is incomplete' really are different questions.
value.receipt: Read at the fix sha from the beee1491..b332f46 diff: the daemon assigns scan_incomplete directly from candidate_limit_exhausted with no other input, and both are emitted into the meta object alongside passes.

value.finding: All four binding precision notes are implemented as specified. (1) admitted_sources relocated below the vector LIMIT — the semi-join is now inside candidate_vectors' WHERE at embeddings.rs:620-625 rather than above the page. (2) BOTH key legs are inside: the raw leg at :622-623 and the smart leg at :624-625, fed by an admitted_sources that unions scope_representatives with smart_content joined on raw_hash at :605-612, so a --source smart search cannot starve in the narrower slot. (3) A distinct carrier exists and survives a non-empty fused page: SearchOutcome gains candidate_limit_exhausted, scan_incomplete and passes (search.rs:186-193) set on ALL THREE exits including the non-empty early return, and http.rs:620-622 publishes them; truncated was correctly left alone. (4) The no-Err change is scoped to search_elements only — the single surviving Err(candidate_limit_exhausted) is at :413 inside the unfiltered query_embeddings, and the constant's doc at :70-73 now states the split explicitly. Additionally admitted_elements and smart_map are bounded to the candidate page (:646, :690-691), which is what produced the large latency win.

value.finding: ac-0001 remains TRUE and the query got dramatically faster. AMENDED after the prod EXPLAIN: this finding originally reported that smart_content is 'now probed once per candidate rather than resolved once' (fixture loops 1 -> 160, exactly at candidate_limit, 'zero margin') and concluded that the plan's goal prose 'smart_content text_hash->raw_hash resolved ONCE' no longer described the shipped statement. THAT CONCLUSION IS WITHDRAWN. On prod the statement's max smart_content Actual Loops is 1, not 160. The 150-160 figure is an artefact of the seeded fixture, in which all 20,000 embeddings share one identical vector and the tables are small enough that a nested loop is the cheapest plan; prod's real vector spread and statistics produce a hash join and a single probe. What survives from the original observation: the bound is genuine and worth asserting (the shipped test asserts loops <= candidate_limit, and the fixture value does vary run to run - 150 and 160 both observed), it was never a correlated SubPlan, and the coder's prose change to 'resolved once per page' is the more precise wording and should be kept. What does not survive: the claim that per-candidate probing is what the shipped statement does, and the 'zero margin' characterisation. The reviewer over-generalised from a fixture that pins plan SHAPE but cannot be read for COST - the third time in this review that this fixture pointed the opposite way from production (the others being the round-1 buffer-count fear, 60,000-75,000 predicted against 8,063 measured, and the round-1 latency figure, 105-121 ms fixture against 35 ms prod). Recorded by o-prime as backlog row 168, fixture realism.

PROD, one guarded EXPLAIN of the same statement (see vd-ac04): Execution Time 35.068 ms, 8,063 shared blocks, three smart_content index-scan nodes at loops 0 / 1 / 1, no correlated SubPlan. value.rationale: ac-0004 TRUE, measured on prod BEFORE the bounce and therefore independent of it — the criterion asks what the shipped statement does against prod's data and statistics, which does not require the new binary to be running. All four thresholds pass with margin, including both reviewer additions o-prime adopted. The HNSW-driver clause was the load-bearing one, because admission moved back inside the ORDER BY/LIMIT as a HASH semi-join, a different cost object from the old correlated EXISTS that the seeded corpus could not settle: the planner keeps the index driver on real prod statistics. This also settles the reviewer's round-1 worry that the fixture understated prod, since the run was the UNSCOPED shape — the profile's reference query and the worst case for admitted_elements (484 MB heap, 264,882 live tuples) — and it touched 8,063 buffers rather than the 60,000-75,000 feared, because the fix bounds admitted_elements and smart_map to the candidate page. SCOPE LIMITS, verbatim, read before citing: '1. One run, from psql, against prod data — not through the daemon and not post-bounce. It measures the statement and the planner's choice on prod statistics; it does not measure the daemon path, connection pooling, or candidate-expansion passes in the running service. 2. ac-0005 is unaffected and still owed — client wall-time, open-job-bracketed, scoped and unscoped interleaved, plus the must-return-results gate. That needs the bounce. 3. The query vector is a real stored embedding sampled from embeddings_1024, not the byte-identical bind from dbprof/explain160.out (which I do not have). So this is the profile's shape — limit=40, candidate_limit=160, unscoped — with a genuine query point, not a byte-exact replay. 4. Two small read-only SELECTs were made to obtain binds: one GROUP BY model_key count, and one LIMIT 1 vector fetch. Disclosed for completeness; nothing written.'
value.receipt: Prod flowspace3-db :5433, database flowspace3, statement = shipped SEARCH_ELEMENTS_SQL at 8d04a77 (byte-identical to b332f46). Guards: BEGIN READ ONLY; SET LOCAL statement_timeout='30s'; SET LOCAL max_parallel_workers_per_gather=0; SET LOCAL hnsw.iterative_scan=strict_order; SET LOCAL jit=off; ONE EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, VERBOSE, FORMAT JSON); ROLLBACK. Preconditions logged: load1 10.51 (10.51/12.59/14.79) below the authorised ceiling of 15, status queue 0, last retention purge 06:05:54Z so none in progress. Nothing written; the old statement was never executed on prod. MEASURED: Execution Time 35.068 ms against a <300 ms threshold; shared hit+read 8,063 (hit 7,709 / read 354) against <100,000; smart_content max Actual Loops 1 against <1,000; embeddings_1024_vector_idx still the driver with Actual Rows 160, zero children, ordered by <=>, loops 1. Supporting shape: zero correlated smart_content SubPlans, zero Materialize-over-elements, candidate_vectors target list exactly four columns with no vector, no JIT node, planning 1.815 ms. Against the before-numbers: profile reference 1,667 ms -> 35.068 ms (48x), buffers 3,853,170 -> 8,063 (478x), smart_content loops 962,792 -> 1; against o-prime's pg_stat_statements mean of 10,696 ms over 132 calls, ~305x. Raw plan retained at .harness/temp/agent/_prod_explain.out (171,538 bytes).

value.rationale: ac-0005 TRUE, measured post-bounce against prod daemon pid 74144 running the reviewed binary. Binary identity was verified functionally rather than assumed: the search envelope carries scan_incomplete and passes and does NOT carry candidate_limit_exhausted, which is the exact signature of f-9c41's carrier with f-5c92's single-key change, so the timings provably ran against 8d04a77/c2f4709. Eight runs, scoped and unscoped interleaved, every threshold met: three main-checkout reference runs at 0.55/0.75/0.61 s against a <1 s bar; the two documented previously-slow queries at 0.69 s and 0.54 s against a <2 s bar; three unscoped doc-heavy runs from /Users/jordanknight/substrate/chainglass at 0.70/0.74/0.45 s against a <5 s bar. The reviewer's added must-return-results gate PASSES 8/8 — every run returned 10 results with scan_incomplete=false and empty_because=null, so none was a fast failure or a silent under-fill. passes=1 on EVERY run is the strongest single signal: the candidate page is satisfied on the first attempt and the expansion loop never engages, which is f-9c41's fix observed working in production rather than inferred. CAVEATS, verbatim: '1. Load was hostile, not quiet - load1 ran 17.93-20.27 across the window. The plan's controlled variable is the open-job count (0-2, far under ~50), which is satisfied, but nobody should read these as best-case numbers; they were taken on a loaded box and are therefore pessimistic. 2. The two 60 s-timeout coder queries are not quoted verbatim anywhere in assets/inputs. I substituted the two slow queries that ARE documented: how does the daemon poll the jobs table for work (recorded at 15.6 s in the profile report) and how does the watcher decide what to ignore (the search_scope_starvation question). If o-prime holds the literal timeout strings, re-running those two is a five-second job. 3. Fresh daemon - pid 74144 had been up about two minutes when R1 ran; R1 was the first query it served and came in at 0.55 s, so no cold-start penalty is hiding in the later runs. 4. These are wall-clock client timings including CLI startup and JSON serialisation, not server-side execution time; the server-side figure is ac-0004's 35.068 ms.' SECOND PASS, taken at o-prime's invitation to wait for load: the identical eight-run protocol was repeated at load1 12.92-12.93 with zero open jobs throughout, against the first pass's 17.93-20.27. All eight passed again with passes=1. Hostile window mean 0.629 s (min 0.45, max 0.75); quiet window mean 0.580 s (min 0.49, max 0.77) - a 7.8% difference of means, inside run-to-run noise, with almost completely overlapping ranges. THE LOAD SENSITIVITY IS GONE, and that is the more important result than either number: ac-0005's whole bracketing protocol exists because search used to be violently load-coupled, the plan citing peer evidence of the same query moving from 156 s to 6 s as queue load changed, which is why queue state was made a controlled variable. That coupling is no longer observable across sixteen runs in two regimes. The controlled variable turned out not to need controlling, which is the strongest available evidence that the fix removed the quadratic term rather than merely shrinking it. Caveat: both windows were sampled on a busy workstation (load1 never below 12.9) with an idle queue (0-2), so this shows insensitivity across the SAMPLED range, not that no coupling could appear at extremes.
